summary: @onereach/orest-vue3 preinstall downloads Bun and executes obfuscated 727KB payload
details: The package declares itself as a Vue3 re-export helper — `dist/index.mjs` is a thin ~10KB shim that forwards ~170 names from `globalThis['Vue3']`. The only substantive install-time code is a dropper chain: `package.json` sets `scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs"`, and `setup.mjs` (itself obfuscated with `_0x...` identifiers) downloads the Bun runtime from a GitHub release, unpacks and chmods it, then invokes it via `execFileSync(bun, [math_init.js])`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB single-line obfuscator.io-style blob using a rotating string-array decoder (`WV8StW` shuffle + `n7gIxM` table + `hc1jfK9` decoder) with no relation to Vue3. Executing the payload through a freshly downloaded alternate JavaScript runtime bypasses Node-based static and dynamic analysis. The mismatch between the package's advertised Vue3 shim purpose and the shipped install-time surface (Bun downloader + obfuscated payload) is characteristic of a masquerading dropper, and the concealed payload runs on the installer's host during `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
